executiveSummary: Surveillance data spanning October 2025 through May 2026 from ECDC and PAHO reveals multiple concurrent disease threats across the Americas and Europe. The most significant concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity with documented human exposure risk, elevated dengue transmission across the Americas, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with continued RSV circulation. Mpox, measles resurgence, yellow fever, and pertussis outbreaks further compound the regional disease burden, while ECDC weekly threat reports from April-May 2026 signal continued European surveillance concerns.
bottomLine: Multiple simultaneous disease threats across the Americas and Europe demand heightened surveillance, with A(H5N1) pandemic preparedness and dengue control remaining the highest-priority actions.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Dual PAHO epidemiological updates in November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained transmission
Animal-to-human spillover risk with reports spanning multiple months
Continued circulation in animal reservoirs across the Americas
threats.action: Enhance animal-human interface surveillance, activate pandemic preparedness protocols, expand PCR testing capacity at veterinary and human health interfaces

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating elevated transmission
Historically high seasonal burden with hyperendemicity in multiple countries
Potential for serotype shift increasing severe dengue risk
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations, activate case management protocols for severe dengue, and issue public health advisories in affected countries

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza
signals: PAHO alert issued 27 April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere season
Previous alert in December 2025 covering Northern Hemisphere season onset
Simultaneous RSV co-circulation flagged in January 2026 alert increasing healthcare burden
threats.action: Accelerate Southern Hemisphere influenza vaccination campaigns, monitor healthcare capacity, and enhance sentinel surveillance for co-circulating respiratory viruses

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 indicating ongoing transmission
Sustained multi-month activity requiring continued continental-level monitoring
Risk of clade Ib importation from African epicenters
threats.action: Maintain ring vaccination programs, strengthen contact tracing networks, and screen returning travelers from high-burden regions

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two sequential PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating persistent resurgence
Multi-country pattern suggesting waning vaccine immunity and surveillance gaps
Elevated risk to unvaccinated infants and immunocompromised populations
threats.action: Review national immunization schedules, accelerate catch-up vaccination programs for children and pregnant women, and enhance clinical recognition training

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 13 March 2026
Enzootic transmission risk in forested border regions
Potential for urban yellow fever if Aedes aegypti exposure occurs in under-vaccinated populations
threats.action: Enforce vaccination requirements for travelers to endemic zones, strengthen epizootic surveillance in primates, and ensure vaccine stockpile adequacy

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 3 February 2026 indicating resurgence
Ongoing global measles resurgence providing importation pressure
COVID-19-era immunization gaps creating susceptible cohorts
threats.action: Conduct vaccination coverage assessments, implement supplementary immunization activities in sub-national areas with coverage below 95%, and activate outbreak response protocols

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 10 February 2026
Co-circulation with dengue complicates clinical diagnosis and case management
Geographic expansion risk in areas with competent Aedes vector populations
threats.action: Strengthen arboviral differential diagnosis capacity, integrate chikungunya into existing dengue vector control programs, and monitor for neurological complications

diseases: Communicable disease threats (multi-pathogen ECDC weekly surveillance)

amrSignals: No direct AMR-specific alerts identified in the 21 reports; however, Bordetella pertussis treatment failures should be monitored for macrolide resistance given resurgence trends
Dengue co-infection burden may drive inappropriate antibiotic use, a secondary AMR risk requiring antimicrobial stewardship messaging
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory threat convergence: influenza A(H5N1) zoonotic spillover risk overlapping with seasonal influenza and RSV co-circulation creates compounded healthcare system stress
Sequential PAHO pertussis alerts (December 2025 and March 2026) indicate a sustained multi-country resurgence not resolved by standard vaccination programs, suggesting immunity gaps
Arboviral co-circulation (dengue, chikungunya) across the Americas in early 2026 increases diagnostic misclassification risk and may undercount true disease burden
ECDC issued five consecutive weekly threat reports from mid-April through mid-May 2026, suggesting sustained or escalating European communicable disease activity requiring further data disclosure
Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome alert in December 2025 combined with rodent-borne disease seasonality may signal environmental or ecological drivers of zoonotic spillover in the Americas
